title: Fallback routing, handshake semantics, KV cache and kernel notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a crunchy, working sketch for how the inference runtime should negotiate request semantics, KV cache usage, kernel compatibility, and fallback routing when capacity or capability mismatches occur. It focuses on the API surface (envelope + error semantics) we expose to callers and the runtime's outbound signals used by the router/scheduler.

Scope:
- Request/response envelope fields we expect clients to set and runtime to return.
- Minimal version negotiation and graceful-ignore rules for forward/back compat.
- Error code taxonomy for routing decisions (retryable vs non-retryable vs fallthrough).
- KV cache handshake mechanics and lightweight cache-id lifecycle.
- Kernel capability advertisement and kernel-selection failure modes.
- Fallback routing semantics (to cheaper model, different region, or degraded streaming mode).

Non-goals:
- Complete scheduler implementation details (this is high-level contract only).
- Deep performance microbenchmarks for KV strategies.

High-level goals:
1) Make it safe for new fields to be added by clients without breaking runtime.
2) Ensure the router can make deterministic fallback decisions using explicit error codes and signals.
3) Minimize round-trips for KV cache warm start.
4) Allow the runtime to reject requests that cannot be served (kernel mismatch) in a way that enables automated fallback.

Request envelope (informal example):
{
  "request_id": "uuid-1234",
  "client_version": "1.4.0",
  "model": "gptx-3-small",
  "model_variant": "int8-fast",
  "seq_len_hint": 1024,
  "priority": "p50",
  "routing_policy": "prefer-low-cost",  // hint to router
  "kv": {
    "cache_key": "user-1234-convo-456",
    "expected_prefix_tokens": 120,
    "allow_prefetch": true
  },
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "stream": false,
  "allow_fallbacks": true,
  "metadata": { /* opaque, runtime may ignore unknown fields */ }
}

Envelope rules and compatibility guarantees:
- Major version bump (x.y.z where x changes) = incompatible: runtime must return error code 4003 (unsupported_protocol_version) for requests it cannot parse or honor.
- Minor/patch bumps: runtime should ignore unknown top-level fields and pass them through in logs (forward-compat).
- Unknown enum values (e.g., new "priority") should default to a safe policy: runtime uses "normal" priority and emits a warning in response.headers.
- Clients may send "kv.cache_key" as empty or omitted. Runtime must treat omission as no-KV-flow and not attempt KV lookups.
- Field deprecation: runtime will accept deprecated field aliases for 12 months and emit deprecation warnings.

KV cache handshake semantics:
- The client may include kv.cache_key and kv.expected_prefix_tokens. When present runtime will attempt to look up a cache entry.
- Runtime responses: on success, include cache_state: "warm" | "partial" | "miss", and cache_id: "cid-...". cache_id is ephemeral; treat as opaque token for subsequent requests.
- If a cache lookup succeeds (warm) runtime should bind the KV shards to the request and return a small telemetry header indicating saved_token_seconds.
- If expected_prefix_tokens > actual cached tokens, runtime returns cache_state: "partial" and an estimate field cached_prefix_available. Client can choose to resend a prefix or continue.
- Prefetch: if allow_prefetch=true and runtime can pre-warm without violating SLOs, it should kick off background fetch and set cache_state: "warming" with an estimated_ready_ms. This is advisory only.
- Cache-id lifecycle: valid for up to 5 minutes by default (configurable per-customer). Cache-ids are namespaced by model_variant and runtime cluster to avoid cross-variant corruption.

Kernel capability and handshake:
- Kernels (execution backends) advertise capability tags at allocation time: attention_types (flash_attn, standard), quant_support (int8, fp16), kv_layout (interleaved, contiguous), max_seq, kv_prefetchable.
- Request routing: runtime should only route requests to kernels whose advertised capabilities satisfy the request constraints (seq_len_hint <= kernel.max_seq, required quant in quant_support, kv_layout compatible with client's cache layout expectation).
- Kernel mismatch behavior: if no compatible kernels in current pool: return error code 1002 (kernel_incompatibility) if allow_fallbacks=false. If allow_fallbacks=true, router tries the following ordered fallbacks: 1) compatible kernel in other pool/region; 2) lower-cost model variant with compatible kernel (if model substitution allowed); 3) degrade to streaming-without-kv mode (if possible). Each fallback attempt should be instrumented and attached to the response metadata (fallback_path: ["region-eu", "model-gptx-3-xq"...]).

Error code taxonomy (proposal):
- 2000: ok (success)
- 3000: client_invalid_request (bad schema / missing required fields)
- 3001: unsupported_protocol_version (major mismatch)
- 1001: capacity_exhausted (no slots in requested capacity tier)  -- router can retry to other pools if allow_fallbacks=true
- 1002: kernel_incompatibility (no kernel meets capability constraints) -- triggers fallback logic
- 1003: kv_lookup_miss (cache absent) -- non-fatal; runtime should still serve request but indicate increased cost
- 1500: transient_internal_error (retryable with backoff)
- 1501: shard_io_error (KV backend I/O) -- route-level decision: try fallback cache shard or skip cache
- 4001: auth_permission_denied
- 5000: internal_server_error (non-retryable without operator intervention)

For each error code we maintain headers/metadata: retryable: true|false, route_hint: "dedicated"|"hosted"|"private", metric_tag: short string. Router/scheduler uses these flags to drive automated retry/fallback.

Response signals for routing/observability:
- response.meta: { served_by: "pool-a-42", kernel_tags: [..], cache_state: "warm" } (we will flatten into response headers in the API)
- telemetry entries: request_path (original), fallback_path (list), attempts, time_to_first_byte_ms, kv_saved_tokens_estimate.

Scheduling considerations (short notes):
- Scheduler should prioritize jobs by priority then by cache_warmth (preferring warm caches to reduce per-token cost), but never starve high priority.
- Batching should be aware of seq_len_hint distribution; kernel selection should pick kernel with best avg-match to batch distribution to reduce padding waste.
- If capacity_exhausted error occurs frequently for a customer, emit a signal to autoscaler to consider pre-warming dedicated capacity.

Failure/fallback flows (examples):
1) Kernel mismatch + allow_fallbacks=true -> router lands on a compatible kernel in a different pool (same region) -> return with fallback_path recorded.
2) KV miss (cache_state: miss) -> runtime serves full KV assemble path; include cost_penalty_estimate header so billing/optimizer can track.
3) Prefetch requested but warming time > threshold -> runtime aborts prefetch and returns cache_state: miss with warming_failed flag; router may choose to retry with a warm pool.

Telemetry and metrics we must surface:
- per-request: cache_hit (bool), cache_state, kernel_id, served_pool, fallback_count, primary_error_code, request_size_tokens, tokens_served
- aggregated: per-variant cache_hit_rate, kernel_incompat_rate, fallback_rate by region

Open questions / TODOs:
- Canonical representation for cache_id and whether clients should be allowed to persist across sessions longer than 5m for offline replay (security/consistency implications).
- How much of the kernel capability vocabulary to expose to clients vs keep internal (leak surface vs helpful for explicit constraints).
- Backcompat policy: exact window for deprecated-field acceptance and on what schedule to enforce breaking changes.
- Define exact header names and limited character sets for route_hint and metric_tag.

Immediate next steps:
- Get buy-in from scheduler and router leads (Arjun, Leah) on error taxonomy and fallback order.
- Prototype cache handshake (cache_id + warming) in a feature branch and test with small traffic. (PR referenced above)
- Add unit tests for unknown-field ignore semantics and enum fallback to ensure forwards compatibility.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally pragmatic and contains several suggestions that trade simplicity for developer ergonomics. If you disagree with any of the fallback ordering or error codes, flag with rationale.

Slack threads / related tickets: #infra-runtime-kv, ENG-4123, PR 871

---
Author note: This is a working sketch. Expect follow-up drafts to split the KV handshake into its own spec and to add exact HTTP header names and example responses once we converge on the error codes.
